/equipment-options/process-control/monit.title: Monitoring / Analytics

This category includes devices and systems that capture real-time process data—such as flow, pressure, shot count, and material presence—to provide visibility into dispensing performance and system behavior.

/equipment-options/process-control/proce.title: Process Control Computer
/equipment-options/process-control/proce.description: Process Control Computers form the core control layer for Kirkco dispensing and metering systems. This category represents the systems responsible for executing dispensing logic, managing recipes, coordinating system components, and maintai
/equipment-options/process-control/proce.overview: Process Control Computers form the core control layer for Kirkco dispensing and metering systems. This category represents the systems responsible for executing dispensing logic, managing recipes, coordinating system components, and maintaining consistent process conditions during production.

/equipment-options/process-control/integ.title: Integration / Automation
/equipment-options/process-control/integ.description: Integration & Automation represents the system layer that connects Kirkco dispensing, metering, and monitoring equipment into coordinated manufacturing workflows. This category focuses on how individual components—such as control computers,
/equipment-options/process-control/integ.overview: Integration & Automation represents the system layer that connects Kirkco dispensing, metering, and monitoring equipment into coordinated manufacturing workflows. This category focuses on how individual components—such as control computers, metering units, and sensors—interface with higher-level automation systems to enable synchronized, repeatable production. Rather than describing standalone devices, Integration & Automation abstracts how Kirkco equipment operates within automated cells, production lines, and factory control architectures. These systems support communication between dispensing hardware and external controls, allowing processes to be triggered, adjusted, and verified as part of broader manufacturing operations.

These systems deliver thick-film corrosion protection and durable surface defense even under harsh conditions.

/equipment-options/polyurethane-processi.title: Industrial Pentane Capable Metering Machines
/equipment-options/polyurethane-processi.description: Pentane capable metering machines are specialized polyurethane foam metering and mixing systems designed to handle hydrocarbon blowing agents like pentane. Unlike standard PU metering machines, these units are engineered to safely meter, mi
/equipment-options/polyurethane-processi.overview: Pentane capable metering machines are specialized polyurethane foam metering and mixing systems designed to handle hydrocarbon blowing agents like pentane. Unlike standard PU metering machines, these units are engineered to safely meter, mix, and dispense formulations that include pentane — enabling high-quality closed-cell foam production with reduced environmental impact. Pentane is commonly used as a blowing agent in rigid and integral skin foams due to its effective foaming characteristics and its suitability for producing high-insulation and structurally robust PU foam.

/equipment-options/polyurethane-processi.title: Urethane Foam Mixing Guns
/equipment-options/polyurethane-processi.description: Urethane foam mixing guns are purpose-built dispense tools used to apply two-component polyurethane foam materials with precise mix quality and accurate control over foam output. These guns integrate metered components, internal mix chamber
/equipment-options/polyurethane-processi.overview: Urethane foam mixing guns are purpose-built dispense tools used to apply two-component polyurethane foam materials with precise mix quality and accurate control over foam output. These guns integrate metered components, internal mix chambers, and ergonomic controls to support a wide range of foam applications — from insulation and core fill to sealing and structural foam tasks. Whether used for insulation, assembly, or production applications, properly configured mixing guns help ensure homogeneous blending and consistent foam performance directly at the point of dispense.

/equipment-options/polyurethane-processi.title: Industrial Low Pressure Metering Polyurethane Equipment
/equipment-options/polyurethane-processi.description: Low-pressure metering refers to systems designed to meter and mix two-component polyurethane materials at moderate pressures, making them ideal for small to medium production runs, low-pressure foams, elastomers, coatings, and C. A. S. E. p
/equipment-options/polyurethane-processi.breadcrumbLeaf: Industrial Low Pressure Metering Polyurethane Equipment
/equipment-options/polyurethane-processi.overview: Low-pressure metering refers to systems designed to meter and mix two-component polyurethane materials at moderate pressures, making them ideal for small to medium production runs, low-pressure foams, elastomers, coatings, and C. A. S. E. polyurethanes (coatings, adhesives, sealants, and elastomers). These machines deliver accurate metering and mixing at lower operating pressures, while handling a broad range of component viscosities and production requirements. Low-pressure metering is often chosen when gentler dispensing is needed — such as when materials are shear-sensitive, require multiple independent stream processing, or when pump wear must be minimized over extended service life.

/equipment-options/polyurethane-processi.title: High-Pressure Polyurethane Metering Systems
/equipment-options/polyurethane-processi.description: High-pressure metering is the industrial standard for the precise delivery, ratio control, and mixing of two-component polyurethane materials. Engineered for demanding production environments, Kirkco’s high-pressure polyurethane metering sy
/equipment-options/polyurethane-processi.overview: High-pressure metering is the industrial standard for the precise delivery, ratio control, and mixing of two-component polyurethane materials. Engineered for demanding production environments, Kirkco’s high-pressure polyurethane metering systems ensure accurate stoichiometric ratios, repeatable shot sizes, and perfectly homogeneous mixing before discharge. Whether you are manufacturing rigid structural foams, continuous elastomers, or microcellular NVH dampening components, our architectures combine robust high-pressure piston pumps, closed-loop VFD/servo controls, and advanced impingement mixing heads to stabilize your throughput and eliminate material variability.

/equipment-options/lubrication/flow-regu.title: Flow Regulation
/equipment-options/lubrication/flow-regu.description: In lubrication and fluid delivery systems, flow regulation ensures that grease, oil, and other fluids move through the system at the right rate — regardless of pressure or pump variation. Stable flow improves performance of downstream meter
/equipment-options/lubrication/flow-regu.overview: In lubrication and fluid delivery systems, flow regulation ensures that grease, oil, and other fluids move through the system at the right rate — regardless of pressure or pump variation. Stable flow improves performance of downstream metering valves, reduces material waste, and enhances repeatability in automated and manual lubrication processes.

/equipment-options/lubrication/pressure-.title: Pressure Control
/equipment-options/lubrication/pressure-.description: In lubrication systems, pressure control and flow regulation components ensure that grease, oil, and other lubricant media are delivered at the correct pressure and flow rate to metering valves, dispensers, and lubrication points. These com
/equipment-options/lubrication/pressure-.overview: In lubrication systems, pressure control and flow regulation components ensure that grease, oil, and other lubricant media are delivered at the correct pressure and flow rate to metering valves, dispensers, and lubrication points. These components stabilize variations from pumps and line resistance, improving the consistency, precision, and reliability of lubrication delivery.

/equipment-options/lubrication/feeding-a.title: Lubricant Feeding and Supply Systems
/equipment-options/lubrication/feeding-a.description: Lubrication feeding and supply systems are engineered to transport greases, oils, and other lubricant materials from storage containers — such as drums, pails, cartridges, or tanks — to lubrication points, metering valves, and dispensing eq
/equipment-options/lubrication/feeding-a.overview: Lubrication feeding and supply systems are engineered to transport greases, oils, and other lubricant materials from storage containers — such as drums, pails, cartridges, or tanks — to lubrication points, metering valves, and dispensing equipment. These systems ensure consistent flow and pressure for reliable machine lubrication, maintenance, and production operations.

/equipment-options/lubrication/dispensin.title: Industrial Lubrication Dispensing Systems
/equipment-options/lubrication/dispensin.description: Apply the right lubricant in the right pattern, volume, and location with dispensing hardware engineered around your process. Kirkco designs lubrication dispensing systems for the controlled application of grease, oil, and other lubricant m
/equipment-options/lubrication/dispensin.overview: Apply the right lubricant in the right pattern, volume, and location with dispensing hardware engineered around your process. Kirkco designs lubrication dispensing systems for the controlled application of grease, oil, and other lubricant media across machinery, assembly stations, maintenance operations, and production lines. Dispensing options support dot or shot application, continuous flow, spray, and time-pressure methods for repeatable material delivery. A complete dispensing system combines the valve with the supply pump, pressure-control equipment, delivery lines, controls, and—when required—flow or pressure monitoring. The result is a dispensing architecture selected around the lubricant, application point, cycle time, dispense pattern, and production environment.

/equipment-options/lubrication/metering.title: Lubrication System Metering
/equipment-options/lubrication/metering.description: Lubrication metering valves are engineered to control and dispense precise amounts of greases, oils, and lubricants in industrial systems where accuracy and repeatability are essential. These valves provide consistent lubrication delivery —
/equipment-options/lubrication/metering.overview: Lubrication metering valves are engineered to control and dispense precise amounts of greases, oils, and lubricants in industrial systems where accuracy and repeatability are essential. These valves provide consistent lubrication delivery — whether in dot (shot), continuous, or spray applications — across manufacturing, assembly, and maintenance operations.

/equipment-options/composites/pultrusion.title: Pultrusion
/equipment-options/composites/pultrusion.description: Pultrusion is a continuous, automated composite manufacturing process used to produce long, straight profiles with a uniform cross‑section and exceptional longitudinal strength and rigidity. The word “pultrusion” combines pull and extrusion
/equipment-options/composites/pultrusion.overview: Pultrusion is a continuous, automated composite manufacturing process used to produce long, straight profiles with a uniform cross‑section and exceptional longitudinal strength and rigidity. The word “pultrusion” combines pull and extrusion — reflecting how reinforcing fibers are pulled through resin and a heated die to form cured composite shapes.

/equipment-options/composites/open-mold-.title: Chopping & Lamination
/equipment-options/composites/open-mold-.description: Kirkco understands the importance of precision when processing multi-component materials. Different systems are required for different materials. There are three mixing systems available to process variances in viscosity, mixture properties
/equipment-options/composites/open-mold-.overview: Kirkco understands the importance of precision when processing multi-component materials. Different systems are required for different materials. There are three mixing systems available to process variances in viscosity, mixture properties, short pot life, etc.

/equipment-options/composites/open-mold-.title: Gel Coat
/equipment-options/composites/open-mold-.description: Gel coat is a specialized resin applied to the surface of a composite mold before reinforcing laminate materials. It cures to form a pigmented, weather-resistant surface that protects the composite part and provides a finished appearance on
/equipment-options/composites/open-mold-.overview: Gel coat is a specialized resin applied to the surface of a composite mold before reinforcing laminate materials. It cures to form a pigmented, weather-resistant surface that protects the composite part and provides a finished appearance once demolded. Gel coats are widely used in open-mold processes, such as hand lay-up and spray lay-up, to deliver cosmetic quality and environmental protection to finished FRP parts.

/equipment-options/composites/open-mold-.title: Open Mold Technology
/equipment-options/composites/open-mold-.description: Open mold technology refers to composite manufacturing processes where reinforcements and resin are applied into an open mold cavity and allowed to cure while exposed to air. This technique offers flexibility for part size and design, and r
/equipment-options/composites/open-mold-.overview: Open mold technology refers to composite manufacturing processes where reinforcements and resin are applied into an open mold cavity and allowed to cure while exposed to air. This technique offers flexibility for part size and design, and remains a widely used method for producing large composite components.

/equipment-options/composites/pull-windi.title: Pull Winding
/equipment-options/composites/pull-windi.description: Pull winding is a continuous composite manufacturing process that combines elements of pultrusion and filament winding to produce hollow, thin-walled profiles with excellent mechanical properties. The process involves winding resin-impregna
/equipment-options/composites/pull-windi.overview: Pull winding is a continuous composite manufacturing process that combines elements of pultrusion and filament winding to produce hollow, thin-walled profiles with excellent mechanical properties. The process involves winding resin-impregnated reinforcements onto a mandrel and pulling them through a heated die, where the resin cures into a solid composite structure.

/equipment-options/composites/filament-w.title: Filament Winding
/equipment-options/composites/filament-w.description: Filament winding is a composite manufacturing process in which continuous fiber reinforcements such as glass, carbon, or aramid are impregnated with resin and wound under tension over a rotating mandrel to create hollow or cylindrical compo
/equipment-options/composites/filament-w.overview: Filament winding is a composite manufacturing process in which continuous fiber reinforcements such as glass, carbon, or aramid are impregnated with resin and wound under tension over a rotating mandrel to create hollow or cylindrical composite parts. The precise control of fiber placement and resin saturation allows the production of components with high structural performance, excellent dimensional control, and minimal waste.

/equipment-options/composites/closed-mol.title: Vacuum Infusion Molding
/equipment-options/composites/closed-mol.description: Vacuum infusion molding (also known as vacuum-assisted resin transfer molding or VIM) is a closed mold composite manufacturing process that uses vacuum pressure to draw resin through dry reinforcement materials contained in a sealed mold. T
/equipment-options/composites/closed-mol.overview: Vacuum infusion molding (also known as vacuum-assisted resin transfer molding or VIM) is a closed mold composite manufacturing process that uses vacuum pressure to draw resin through dry reinforcement materials contained in a sealed mold. The vacuum pulls catalyzed resin through the reinforcement layers, resulting in uniform fiber wet-out and parts with excellent structural integrity and surface finish.

/equipment-options/composites/closed-mol.title: Resin Transfer Molding
/equipment-options/composites/closed-mol.description: Resin Transfer Molding (RTM) is a closed mold composite manufacturing process in which dry reinforcement materials such as fiberglass or carbon fiber are placed into a sealed mold cavity, and catalyzed resin is injected under pressure to fu
/equipment-options/composites/closed-mol.overview: Resin Transfer Molding (RTM) is a closed mold composite manufacturing process in which dry reinforcement materials such as fiberglass or carbon fiber are placed into a sealed mold cavity, and catalyzed resin is injected under pressure to fully impregnate the reinforcement and cure into a finished part. This closed mold environment helps control material flow, improve fiber wet-out, and produce parts with consistent thickness and superior surface finish on both sides.

/equipment-options/composites/closed-mol.title: Resin Injection Molding
/equipment-options/composites/closed-mol.description: Resin injection molding is a closed mold process in composite manufacturing where material is injected under pressure into a sealed mold cavity containing dry reinforcement materials. This enables consistent part quality, high fiber wet-out
/equipment-options/composites/closed-mol.overview: Resin injection molding is a closed mold process in composite manufacturing where material is injected under pressure into a sealed mold cavity containing dry reinforcement materials. This enables consistent part quality, high fiber wet-out, and excellent surface finish, while minimizing air entrapment and defects commonly found in open mold techniques. Closed mold methods also reduce volatile emissions and improve worker safety.

/equipment-options/composites/closed-mol.title: Closed Mold Technology
/equipment-options/composites/closed-mol.description: Closed mold technology refers to composite manufacturing processes in which reinforcement materials are enclosed in a sealed mold cavity and resin is introduced under controlled pressure or vacuum. This approach produces parts with tight di
/equipment-options/composites/closed-mol.overview: Closed mold technology refers to composite manufacturing processes in which reinforcement materials are enclosed in a sealed mold cavity and resin is introduced under controlled pressure or vacuum. This approach produces parts with tight dimensional control, excellent surface quality, and repeatable mechanical properties compared to open mold methods.

Electrically driven or servo-controlled gear pumps provide continuous, pulse-free output with fine speed adjustment, enabling precise ratio and flow control in demanding production environments.

/equipment-options/adhesives-sealants/sm.description: At Kirkco Corporation, we engineer precision metering and dispensing systems that elevate the quality and efficiency of composite manufacturing. Our specialized equipment for Sheet Molding Compound (SMC) and In-Mold Coating (IMC) processes

Our specialized equipment for Sheet Molding Compound (SMC) and In-Mold Coating (IMC) processes empowers manufacturers to produce lightweight, high-strength composite parts with flawless, paint-ready surfaces straight out of the press. By integrating our advanced IMC Coatec metering systems into your compression molding workflow, you can eliminate costly secondary surface preparation, reduce cycle times, and consistently achieve the "Class A" surface finishes demanded by the automotive, commercial vehicle, and recreational marine industries.

/equipment-options/adhesives-sealants/to.breadcrumbLeaf: Tooling Paste & Seamless Modeling Paste Systems

Our equipment is engineered to support controlled material delivery from standard containers, consistent blending, smooth application, and repeatable production workflows. The tooling paste portfolio includes the GP 401 TPD and Eldo-Mix 401T & Tooling Mix, systems identified by Kirkco for pasty two-component materials such as polyurethanes, epoxy resins, and microball-filled materials.

/equipment-options/adhesives-sealants/tw.title: Two-Component Adhesive Metering & Mixing Systems

Kirkco designs two-component equipment for industrial adhesives and sealants that require controlled metering, reliable mixing, and repeatable dispensing. From continuous-flow bonding and sealing to shot dispensing, potting, encapsulation, coating, and molding, Kirkco helps manufacturers select a system architecture that aligns material behavior with production requirements. Our platform supports multi-component materials including epoxies, polyurethanes, silicones, and filled systems, with technology options spanning gear metering, piston metering, shot metering, mixing valves, progressive-cavity metering, and liquid silicone rubber processing.
